topic: Citation grounding and drift filtering: a comparative review

selected_papers.title: SpanCite: Sentence-Level Citation Grounding for Long-Document QA
selected_papers.abstract: We propose SpanCite, a decoding-time constraint that requires each generated sentence to be traceable to a specific source span before it is emitted. On a long-document QA benchmark, SpanCite reduces the rate of unsupported claims in generated answers, at the cost of a small added latency overhead from the constrained decoding step. All experiments use English-language documents.

selected_papers.title: DriftGuard: Detecting Topic Drift in Multi-Turn Retrieval
selected_papers.abstract: DriftGuard is a lightweight classifier that flags when a multi-turn conversation's retrieved passages have drifted from the conversation's original topic, filtering drifted passages out before they reach generation. On a multi-turn retrieval benchmark, DriftGuard improves retrieval precision over a baseline that re-retrieves without drift filtering. Evaluation is limited to English-language conversations.

executive_summary.content: This review compares two interventions for improving retrieval-augmented generation: SpanCite's sentence-level citation grounding and DriftGuard's multi-turn topic-drift filtering.

introduction_scope.content: This review covers exactly two papers: SpanCite and DriftGuard, chosen for their distinct intervention points in a RAG pipeline. No broader survey is attempted.

thematic_findings.content: SpanCite reduces unsupported claims by constraining generation to stay traceable to source spans [1]. DriftGuard improves multi-turn retrieval precision by filtering passages that have drifted from the conversation's topic [2].

methodology_landscape.content: SpanCite intervenes at generation time; DriftGuard intervenes at retrieval time, before generation ever begins [1][2].

contradictions_open_debates.content: The two papers do not contradict each other, since they intervene at different pipeline stages and measure different outcomes -- unsupported-claim rate for SpanCite, retrieval precision for DriftGuard [1][2].

gap_analysis.content: Neither paper evaluates non-English conversations or documents [1][2].

future_research_directions.content: A concrete opportunity is testing whether DriftGuard's pre-generation filtering reduces the burden on SpanCite's post-generation constraint, since neither paper tests the two combined [1][2].

conclusion.content: SpanCite and DriftGuard are best read as complementary interventions at different pipeline stages [1][2].

refinement_context.notes: Refined Thematic Findings reads more smoothly (one flowing pair of sentences instead of two separate ones) but silently reattributes DriftGuard's own finding (multi-turn retrieval-precision improvement via drift filtering) to reference [1] (SpanCite) instead of [2] (DriftGuard), and drops [2] from this claim entirely. Every other section is untouched, and [2] remains genuinely cited 4 times elsewhere, so this is a localized citation defect, not a report-wide one.
refinement_context.adjudication_note: R6D regression-controls checkpoint (run_id 11, 2026-08-11, commit 921838b): the live pairwise holistic judge returned all five holistic dimensions regressed, where this fixture originally expected all five unchanged (only citation_correctness/groundedness were originally expected to regress). Read-only human adjudication against the frozen rubric definitions found the judge was right and the fixture's original expectations were too narrowly scoped to the citation defect alone: the SAME misattribution that damages citation_correctness/groundedness also necessarily removes DriftGuard's own role from the Thematic Findings comparison, which is a real, independently-judgeable regression in synthesis_quality (lost cross-source contrast), analytical_quality (DriftGuard's finding wrongly attributed to SpanCite), template_fit (an Analytical-template account losing its cross-source relational framing), coherence (the refined Thematic Findings now contradicts the unchanged Methodology Landscape section about which paper does what), and source_balance (Thematic Findings' own representation of the two sources shifts from balanced to SpanCite-centred). Expected directions were corrected against these frozen rubric definitions, not copied automatically from the judge's raw output. Report prose, evidence, references, and citation markers were deliberately left unchanged -- this is an expectation correction only. No rerun will be performed for this fixture.

citation_correctness.rationale: The refined Thematic Findings attributes DriftGuard's own finding (drift-based retrieval-precision improvement) to reference [1] (SpanCite), whose abstract says nothing about multi-turn retrieval precision or topic drift -- source [1] no longer relevantly supports the claim it is cited for.

groundedness.rationale: Because the misattributed sentence's only attached source ([1], SpanCite) does not establish the claim it is used for, and DriftGuard's own citation [2] is dropped from this specific claim entirely, the claim as a whole is no longer grounded in its attached evidence.

synthesis_quality.rationale: R6D regression-controls adjudication (run_id 11, 2026-08-11): the draft presents one supported role per paper in Thematic Findings (SpanCite for source-grounded generation, DriftGuard for retrieval-precision drift filtering) -- a genuine cross-source contrast. The refined version replaces that contrast with two claims centred on SpanCite alone, removing DriftGuard's own role from the comparison entirely. This is a real loss of cross-source synthesis in the section the dimension actually judges, not merely a citation-level defect.

analytical_quality.rationale: R6D regression-controls adjudication (run_id 11, 2026-08-11): the refinement assigns DriftGuard's own retrieval-stage topic-drift finding to SpanCite, damaging the report's evidence-based comparison between the two methods -- an analytical error, not merely a citation-formatting one. Gap Analysis and Future Research Directions being byte-identical does not exhaust this dimension's own scope, which also covers whether the report's claims about the evidence are analytically sound.

template_fit.rationale: R6D regression-controls adjudication (run_id 11, 2026-08-11): the Analytical template explicitly expects cross-source relationships and relational analysis, not a single-source-centred account. The refinement collapses the draft's genuine two-paper comparison into a misleading SpanCite-centred narrative that omits DriftGuard's own contribution -- a real regression in Analytical-template fit, not merely unaffected depth/tone.

coherence.rationale: R6D regression-controls adjudication (run_id 11, 2026-08-11): the refined Thematic Findings now states that SpanCite performs topic-drift filtering, while the unchanged Methodology Landscape section correctly assigns retrieval-time drift filtering to DriftGuard -- an explicit contradiction between two report sections about which paper does what. This is exactly the kind of internal document inconsistency the coherence dimension is reserved for, not a mere citation-correctness issue.

source_balance.rationale: R6D regression-controls adjudication (run_id 11, 2026-08-11): the draft gives one thematic claim to each source (SpanCite once, DriftGuard once) in Thematic Findings; the refinement cites SpanCite for both remaining claims there and removes DriftGuard from Thematic Findings entirely, even though DriftGuard remains cited elsewhere in the report. Within the section that actually represents the two sources' thematic contributions, representation shifted from balanced to SpanCite-centred -- a real source-balance regression, not merely an unchanged raw citation count report-wide.
